title: Speaker endorses 22 Amendment
byline: Speaker Jagath Wickramaratne has endorsed the 22nd Amendment to the Constitution today, a statement from the Parliament Media Unit said.

title: Judicature Amendment Bill approved by Parliament
byline: The Judicature Amendment Bill was approved by Parliament by a two-thirds majority with 158 MPs voting for and 62 against.

title: Lanka Sathosa reduces prices of six essential food items
byline: Lanka Sathosa Limited announced a reduction in the prices of six essential food items, effective from tomorrow (September 26).

title: Parliament approves third reading of 22A
byline: Parliament approved the third reading of the 22nd Amendment by a two-thirds majority, with 158 members voting in favour and 63 against.

title: Parliament approves second reading of 22A
byline: Parliament approved the second reading of the 22nd Amendment to the Constitution by a two-thirds majority, with 158 MPs voting in favour and 63 against.

title: A few Opposition MPs will support 22A: Chief Government Whip
byline: A few Opposition MPs will vote in favour of the 22nd Amendment to the Constitution, Chief Government Whip Nalinda Jayatissa said.

title: Red landslide warnings issued for several districts
byline: The National Building Research Organisation (NBRO) has issued the highest-level landslide evacuation warning for several areas in Galle, Kandy and Nuwara Eliya districts amid continued heavy rainfall and an increased risk of landslides.

title: ITAK could have approved 22A if it was part of new Constitution
byline: The Ilankai Tamil Arasu Katchchi (ITAK) could have voted for the 22 Amendment to the Constitution if it had been brought as a part of a new Constitution, MP Shanakiyan Rasamanickam told Parliament today.

title: Chamara Sampath’s ex-private secretary further remanded
byline: Colombo Chief Magistrate Asanga S. Bodaragama today ordered that the former Private Secretary to former Minister Chamara Sampath Dassanayake, who was arrested over an alleged corruption offence, be further remanded till October 9.

title: Zelensky says Trump has made ‘final decision’ to allow Kyiv to make Patriot missiles
byline: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky said Friday that US President Donald Trump will allow Ukraine to manufacture Patriot missiles, a key demand as Kyiv tries to fend off relentless Russian aerial attacks.

title: Ex-Deputy Minister Sarana Gunawardena’s wife remanded
byline: Chinari Lakmanthi Hettiarachchi, the wife of former Deputy Minister Sarana Gunawardena, who was arrested over allegations of offering a bribe, was ordered to be remanded until October 6 by Colombo Chief Magistrate Asanga S. Bodaragama.

title: Saudi Arabia allies line up support as Houthi attacks mount
byline:
Saudi Arabia’s allies are rallying to support the country as the Houthi rebels step up attacks.

France confirmed on Friday that it is sending troops to guard the major oil terminal at Yanbu. Meanwhile, Saudi officials are meeting with peers from Pakistan and Turkiye to discuss options under their mutual defence pact.French President Emmanuel Macron told broadcasters TF1 and France 2 that Paris is to send “soldiers, radars, and defence systems”

title: Former Minister’s ex-private secretary further remanded
byline: Colombo Chief Magistrate Asanga S. Bodaragama today ordered that the former Private Secretary to former Minister Chamara Sampath Dassanayake, who was arrested over an alleged corruption offence, be further remanded till October 9.

title: Sarana Gunawardena’s wife arrested over Rs. 50,000 bribe
byline: The Commission to Investigate Allegations of Bribery or Corruption (CIABOC) has arrested Chinari Lakmanthi Hettiarachchi, the wife of former Deputy Minister Sarana Gunawardena, over an alleged attempt to influence ongoing court proceedings involving her husband.

title: ‘Source of anxiety’: Pakistan cracks down before march to free Imran Khan
byline: The motorway linking Pakistan’s capital with Peshawar, about 180km (110 miles) to the northwest, has been closed to all traffic until further notice, according to a police notification.

title: India to make fastest-ever bullet train to match Japan’s E10
byline: India is getting closer to having its own high-speed bullet train, as Railways are working on the B35, a train designed to reach speeds of up to 350 kmph. The project is part of India’s plan to develop more railway technology at home and reduce its dependence on foreign technology.

title: Former Buddhasasana Ministry Secretary arrested over Rs. 4.7 Mn corruption case
byline: The Commission to Investigate Allegations of Bribery or Corruption (CIABOC) today arrested former Secretary to the Ministry of Buddhasasana, Muthubandage Kamal Bandara Dissanayake, over an alleged corruption case involving government book-printing contracts.

title: Navy seizes drugs worth over Rs. 55 Billion this year
byline: The Sri Lanka Navy has seized illicit drugs estimated to be worth more than Rs. 55 billion through maritime and coastal anti-narcotics operations conducted so far this year, Navy Spokesman Commander Chaminda Walakuluge said.

title: Indian High Commissioner meets Ranil Wickremesinghe
byline: Indian High Commissioner to Sri Lanka Santosh Jha met former President Ranil Wickremesinghe at his political office on Flower Road, Colombo, this morning (25).

title: 20 more forests to be gazetted as reserves tomorrow
byline: Twenty more forests covering nearly 9,538 hectares in six districts are scheduled to be declared forest reserves tomorrow (26) under the Government’s ‘Vanaspathi’ national programme aimed at protecting Sri Lanka’s forest ecosystems for future generations.

title: TIN certificate mandatory for key transactions from November 1
byline: The Inland Revenue Department (IRD) said that submitting a valid Taxpayer Identification Number (TIN) Certificate will become mandatory for a wide range of essential financial, commercial, and administrative transactions with effect from November 1, 2026.

title: Ex-Lanka Mineral Sands Chairman arrested over alleged corruption
byline: The Commission to Investigate Allegations of Bribery or Corruption (CIABOC) today arrested the former Chairman of Lanka Mineral Sands Limited, Udeni Jayaratne Dassanayake, over an alleged corruption case involving the recruitment of casual workers.

title: Ruling party MPs urged to vote according to conscience
byline: Civil society organisation Dinana Dakuna today urged ruling party MPs to vote according to their conscience when Parliament votes on the 22nd Amendment to the Constitution today.

title: Opposition MPs wear black in Parliament
byline: Opposition MPs arrived in Parliament dressed in black today, reportedly in protest against the 22nd Amendment to the Constitution.

title: Netanyahu defends Israeli military action as delegates walk out before UN speech
byline: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu has fiercely defended his country’s military campaigns in Iran, Gaza and elsewhere in the Middle East in a speech to the UN General Assembly.

title: Sri Lanka beat England to level ODI series
byline: Sri Lanka fought back brilliantly to defeat England by 16 runs in the second ODI at Headingley on September 24, levelling the three-match series 1-1. The victory came after Sri Lanka had lost the opening match and now sets up a decisive final ODI at The Oval on Sunday.

title: US airlines oppose China’s bid to add more flights
byline: The head of industry group Airlines for America said on Thursday that US carriers ​oppose adding more direct flights from China to the United States even as Chinese ‌President Xi Jinping raised the idea.
